```{r,echo=FALSE}

while(T){
    part = sample(1:199,1)
    whole = sample(1:199,1)
    perc = part/whole*100
    if(perc%%1==0 && perc<100 && whole != 100 && perc!=50){break}
}

```

Question
========

A store's wholesale cost is $`r whole` per trinket. To calculate the retail price, the store adds a markup. If the retail price is $`r (1+perc/100)*whole`, then what was the markup **percentage**?

(Include the `%` in your answer, no spaces.)

Solution
========

This scenario represents a percent increase. We can find the markup amount by subtracting the two amounts.

$$`r part+whole`-`r whole`=`r part`$$

Now we can find what percent is this markup out of the wholesale cost.

$$\frac{`r part`}{`r whole`}~=~`r perc/100`~=~`r perc`\%$$

The alternative route is to divide the retail price by the wholesale cost to find the scale factor.

$$\frac{`r part+whole`}{`r whole`}=`r (part+whole)/whole`$$

And subtract 1 to find the percent increase.


$$\frac{`r part+whole`}{`r whole`}-1~=~`r perc`\%$$
